items.note: Design-course exercise in which every participant received an AI-generated image stimulus during group ideation; external evaluators rated novelty and usefulness of the 18 best ideas and traced their inspiration source, but no condition differed in AI assistance (no comparison group).

ICIS 2023 short paper describing an experimental series where people develop ideas with generative AI whose feedback modality (numeric vs visual) and timing are manipulated (ai_design); may be a research-in-progress design without results; related to the later Gordetzki et al. ISR paper.

Experiment with three sequential creativity tasks finding AI usage enhances creative performance but biases self- and other-evaluations, with effects persisting immediately after and one week later without AI (possible after_ai); AOM proceedings abstract, N not stated.

180 participants brainstormed solutions with AI assistants holding different values (AI-vs-AI configuration); ideas reflected the AI's values and self-rated quality did not differ, so it is unclear whether any creativity or diversity outcome is scored on the output; arXiv 2402.12814 is the same work.

System paper (MetaEmbody) with an N=20 user study in which design outcomes got higher novelty and feasibility ratings, apparently against a comparison condition (likely baseline AI tool); below the 50-participant threshold.

Online experiment with 298 participants ideating with DALL-E 2 images, traditional art, or no art as stimuli; originality and number of ideas scored (ideas_supplied/stimulus design; AI vs active aid vs none).
Classroom 6-3-5 ideation workshop where student groups could use ChatGPT, Google, or no support; novelty of outputs analyzed (AI ideas more novel); assignment method and N not stated, likely small.

Lab experiment with 60 two-person teams (120 people) assigned to unequal, full, or no GenAI access for a press-release writing task; task quality (search notes say expert-rated originality) scored; the abstract says 'assigned' without stating random; ASIS&T 2025 short paper (10.1002/pra2.1437) is a related version.

System paper (POET) that diversifies text-to-image outputs, evaluated with 28 users across four creative domains; reports higher perceived diversity and fewer prompts, likely versus a baseline tool, but the diversity measure may be perception-based; arXiv 2504.13392 is the same work.

Field experiment with nearly 100 Egyptian senior students who wrote three graded essays with or without ChatGPT, then played an unaided lab innovation game (after_ai), where the ChatGPT group scored 0.6-0.72 SD lower; random assignment not stated in abstract; bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2024.04.03.588037 is the same study.
